To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
manual rupture and transvaginous aspiration of allantoic fluid in multiple pregnancies are both efficient methods of reducing embryo numbers in cows.

manual rupture and transvaginous ultrasound-guided aspiration were equally efficient for reducing the number of fetuses in cows with multiple pregnancies, with a pregnancy loss rate of 46.7 and 62.5% respectively.
manual rupture and transvaginous aspiration of allantoic-amniotic fluid are effective embryo reduction techniques to maintain pregnancy in dairy cows with multiple pregnancies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of two techniques for embryo reduction (manual rupture of the amniotic sac and ultrasound-guided aspiration) in multiple pregnancies in dairy cattle.
embryo reduction in cattle and its effect on pregnancy maintenance.
the development of an embryo reduction technique for multiple pregnancies that could be used in dairy cattle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the type of pregnancy (unilateral vs. bilateral twins) was the only factor affecting pregnancy maintenance in dairy cattle carrying multiple pregnancies.
the type of pregnancy is the most significant factor affecting pregnancy loss following embryo reduction.
the use of a 17G needle for TUGA is not recommended in cattle carrying multiple pregnancies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
embryo reduction is a viable option for dairy cows with multiple pregnancies and that the technique used (MR or TUGA) has little impact on pregnancy maintenance.

manual rupture of the allanto-amniotics sacs of multiple pregnancies is an efficient technique to reduce the number of fetuses, with the risk of pregnancy losses being similar to the risk observed in the control group of cows with single pregnancies.
TUGA with a 22G needle is the method of choice for embryo reduction in cattle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the technique for embryo reduction is not the most important factor to consider when performing embryo reduction in cattle.
embryo reduction is a safe and efficient technique for maintaining pregnancies in dairy cattle.
TUGA is a safe and reliable method for embryo reduction in multiple pregnancies in dairy cattle.
